articles.title: Designing a kill switch for AI agents: what it should stop, and how to know it works
articles.excerpt: Most incident runbooks for software have a step that says "roll back" or "turn off the feature flag". Agent systems need an equivalent that is faster and blunter: stop every agent in the organization,…
articles.body: Most incident runbooks for software have a step that says "roll back" or "turn off the feature flag". Agent systems need an equivalent that is faster and blunter: stop every agent in the organization, now, and keep them stopped until a person decides otherwise. It sounds simple. In practice teams discover during their first real incident that "stop the agents" means a dozen different processes in a dozen places, some of which retry happily when told to stop. This post covers what a kill switch should do, who should hold it, how client code should behave when it is on, and how to test that it works before you need it. When you would pull it You will not use a kill switch often, and that is the point.
articles.author: Sandscale

articles.title: GBase Database: Understanding Backslash Continuation in UNL Export Files
articles.excerpt: The first time I opened a .unl file exported from GBase Database(GBase 8s), I thought the data was corrupted. Some lines ended with a backslash, and the content continued on the next line. It turned o…
articles.body: The first time I opened a .unl file exported from GBase Database(GBase 8s) , I thought the data was corrupted. Some lines ended with a backslash, and the content continued on the next line. It turned out to be intentional. In GBase Database, a backslash at the end of an exported line can indicate that the record continues on the next line. Understanding this behavior is important when working with UNL files, especially when exporting data containing multiline fields such as addresses, comments, or descriptions. 1. Why Does a UNL File Contain a Backslash? Consider this example: 1001|Zhang San|No.1 Zhongguancun Street, Haidian\ Building A|2026-01-08 1002|Li Si|Pudong New Area, Shanghai|2026-01-09 The first record spans two physical lines.

You buy a file, and then you hope it means what the seller says it means. We think that model is dead. If data is going to be infrastructure — electricity-like, token-like, metered per call — then every record has to come with two things: a verdict and reproducible evidence . This post is the public changelog of G-Trusted Data Center , our data factory for MCP/Agent security intelligence. Every asset below is anchored and independently checkable. We published the constitution first: Trusted Data = Verdict + Reproducible Evidence. The four pillars 1. Census — the exposure surface.

articles.title: Bit Length Is Not a Format: Five 34-Bit Layouts
articles.excerpt: Ask someone in the trade for "the 34-bit Wiegand format" and you will usually get one answer: 16 bits of facility code, 16 bits of card number, two parity bits. That answer is right for the credential…
articles.body: Ask someone in the trade for "the 34-bit Wiegand format" and you will usually get one answer: 16 bits of facility code, 16 bits of card number, two parity bits. That answer is right for the credential in their hand and wrong for the one on the next door. Thirty-four bits is a length. A length constrains how many bits arrive; it says nothing about where the fields sit. In the published tables there are five layouts sharing that length, from four vendors, and two of them overlap in a way that produces a facility code nobody will question until a cardholder is standing at a door that will not open. This is not a curiosity. It is the single most common way a working decoder returns a confidently wrong answer. The five The most widespread is HID H10306, also documented by Honeywell as N10002.

articles.body: In Natural Language Processing (NLP) , " hallucination " refers to a phenomenon in which an artificial intelligence model generates text that is grammatically coherent but contains fabricated data, contradicts the provided source material, or is factually incorrect in the real world. Although the public became aware of this behavior with the popularization of conversational assistants based on Large Language Models (LLMs) in late 2022, researchers had been studying it for years in machine translation and news summarization systems. Research studies, such as "Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation" by Ziwei Ji et al. (2023) and a review by Lei Huang et al.

articles.title: AI Audit Evidence, Part 7: A Status Is Not a Receipt
articles.excerpt: We build a runtime that lets AI agents take real write actions inside enterprise systems: create a record, send a request to another service. Every action carries permissions, approvals, and a record…
articles.body: We build a runtime that lets AI agents take real write actions inside enterprise systems: create a record, send a request to another service. Every action carries permissions, approvals, and a record someone can review afterwards. After an authorization is revoked, it can hand over three layers of record: what allowed the request, whether the in-flight call stopped, and whether the effect that already landed at the target is still there. This piece is about the third — reconciliation. An audit needs to know whether the write happened at all. "It did not" and "it did, and was later erased" are different things; when they cannot be told apart, the record writes two events as one sentence — a status is not a receipt. An outbound write times out.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989.
